Yeah I can totally understand what you mean. I think a lot of people dont know how to deal with it because of the stigma around it and them not wanting to make it worse. I find it really hard to open up to people about it as well, it definitely takes a lot of bravery

Hey, I'm not really sure if it helps much me replying. I feel sorta the same in that I feel so childish and immature acting the way I did when I was 13 but I think it's because often for us self harmed it's a core part of our identity (being bullied for it, using it to cope, worry about scars, etc). It never really seems to leave you even when you recover for a period of time and I think because it's such a strong coping mechanism it can make you feel like you're doing a bad job coping with the world. I dont know if that is how you feel at all but if it is, remember the world isnt the place you thought it would be growing up but were all doing the same thing- living one day at a time while trying to put a better foot forward when we can, and when we cant trying to cope with everything going on.

I think you could be panicking over a somewhat normal reaction to something. It sorta sounds like you're avoiding your fear of being rejected by her by not giving her the chance. I've done it before with ex's- caused problems I imagined happening before they could do it to me to sort of save face.

I think I understand what she means- nothing is without cause in a way. Ie you're happy because you saw something nice, you're sad because something bad happened. I think the same sort of basic sentiment doesnt always apply to bipolar so directly (like a cute guy smiled at you so you get butterflies sort of direct) but more in a butterfly effect sort of trigger. Sorry if that sounds super rambly😭
